text: Lesson 13 found a reproducible symptom and a strong lead. This lesson confirms it with real Snowflake tooling, not a hunch — starting with the single most important check, the one that's easy to skip because it feels too obvious.

SHOW TASKS, listing every Task that currently exists. If the design called for exactly one Task doing Finance's job, and this list shows two, that's not a hypothesis anymore. In this scenario, that's exactly what it reveals: alongside finance_refund_task, a second, almost identically named Task, created weeks earlier during a tweak, left running, never suspended.
TASK_HISTORY confirms it precisely. Both Tasks show succeeded runs, on the same five-minute schedule, with start times close enough together that their executions genuinely overlapped.

Here's the full mechanics. A Stream's offset only advances when a committing DML statement reads it. Until that commit, the Stream's unconsumed rows stay visible to any transaction reading it — including a second Task's MERGE, running in an overlapping window. Both Tasks saw the same rows, and both independently satisfied their own WHEN NOT MATCHED condition. ticket_facts_sync_task was never duplicated, which is exactly why Support's numbers stayed correct the entire time.

Nothing about the duplicate Task's own MERGE logic is wrong in isolation — the bug is that two copies of the same consumer existed at once, an operational leftover, not a formula mistake. Next lesson removes it and proves the fix actually held.
